item.text: {"text":"T5 provides direct prior art for learned, head-specific scalar biases added to attention logits according to query–key relative distance. Its position buckets distinguish nearby offsets precisely and group larger distances logarithmically; bias parameters are shared across layers. Bidirectional bucketing distinguishes the two directions. This mechanism is established architecture, rather than a new positional encoding contribution. [T5 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683), [implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/t5/modeling_t5.py).\n\nBERT4Rec originally adds learned absolute position embeddings to item embeddings, trains with masked-item prediction under bidirectional attention, and appends a mask for next-item inference. TiSASRec establishes related recommendation-specific precedent by combining absolute positions with pairwise elapsed-time representations; elapsed time differs from sequence-index distance, and its mechanism is not simply T5’s scalar bias. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690), [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf). Assessment: adding T5-style bidirectional relative bias to BERT4Rec is a reasonable controlled adaptation, with potential benefits requiring validation; these sources do not establish novelty or guaranteed improvement. Compare absolute positions alone, relative bias alone, and both together while preserving masked-target training, appended-mask inference, and one jointly trained model per category. Position-only bias needs no timestamps; actual time-gap features should be evaluated separately."}
